quote: To will oneself free is also to will others free.
source: Simone de Beauvoir, The Ethics of Ambiguity, Part II, Personal Freedom and Others (trans. Bernard Frechtman, 1948)

evidence.where: The Frechtman translation hosted in full by the Marxists Internet Archive, chapter II, headed Personal Freedom and Others; the sentence stands in the final paragraph of that part, directly after the reply to the charge that existentialism is a formal doctrine, and is followed by This will is not an abstract formula
evidence.edition: The Ethics of Ambiguity, trans. Bernard Frechtman (New York: Philosophical Library, 1948), from Pour une morale de l'ambiguité, 1947
evidence.locator: Part II, Personal Freedom and Others, final paragraph

reason: The wording is Frechtman's and the part and section are as proposed. The line is a sentence of Beauvoir's own argument, not a character's, so no speaker is named. Beauvoir stands at one of three for the year.
